r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped service dependencies and retrieved 7-day change log for all services. auth-service depends on user-db, redis-session, and otp-provider. A deploy of auth-service v7.1.3 occurred at 13:05 on 2026-10-13.

findings.statement: auth-service depends synchronously on otp-provider, user-db, and redis-session.
notification-service depends on sms-vendor and event-bus.
auth-service was deployed at 2026-10-13T13:05:00+00:00 with summary 'auth-service v7.1.3: limit OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes'.

open_questions: Did the code change in auth-service v7.1.3 introduce a bug or interact incorrectly with otp-provider?

r1-observability-1.summary: Login failures and OTP delivery issues started precisely at 2026-10-13T13:40:00+00:00 due to upstream 503 errors from otp-provider called by auth-service.

findings.statement: auth-service error rate spiked to 34.07% starting at 2026-10-13T13:40:00+00:00.
mobile-bff error rate increased to 3.98% starting at 2026-10-13T13:41:00+00:00.
auth-service logs show repeated OTP send failures because otp-provider responded with 503 Service Unavailable, first seen at 2026-10-13T13:40:13+00:00.

open_questions: Why did otp-provider begin returning 503 Service Unavailable errors at 13:40?

r2-observability-1.summary: External dependency otp-provider experienced a severe failure starting at 13:40, showing an error rate anomaly peaking at 80.04% and a p99 latency anomaly jumping to 5495 ms. This directly correlates with the auth-service failure logs and the user-facing login errors.

findings.statement: otp-provider error rate spiked starting at 13:40, going from a baseline of 0.3% to a peak of 80.04% at 13:52.
otp-provider p99 latency spiked starting at 13:40, going from a baseline of 907.65 ms to a peak of 5495.16 ms at 13:56.
otp-provider request rate remained stable with no traffic anomalies during the incident window.
otp-provider does not produce internal logs accessible via the query_logs tool.

open_questions: What caused otp-provider to experience high latency and service unavailability starting at 13:40?

hypotheses.title: External Third-Party Outage: otp-provider Service Degradation
hypotheses.mechanism: The external otp-provider suffered an internal degradation or outage starting at 13:40, resulting in high latency and 503 Service Unavailable errors. Because auth-service has a synchronous dependency on otp-provider, authentication requests failed to send OTPs, causing an error rate spike in auth-service and cascading error rate increases in mobile-bff.

supporting.note: auth-service error rate spiked sharply from 0.33% to ~33.65% starting precisely at 13:40.
otp-provider error rate spiked from baseline 0.3% to a peak of 80.04% at 13:52, starting precisely at 13:40.
otp-provider p99 latency jumped from 907.65 ms to 5495.16 ms starting at 13:40.
auth-service logs explicitly show OTP send failures because otp-provider responded with 503 Service Unavailable starting at 13:40:13.
mobile-bff error rate increased starting at 13:41 due to its synchronous dependency on auth-service.

contradicting.note: otp-provider request rate remained completely stable with no traffic surges or volume anomalies during the incident window.

assumptions: The external vendor (otp-provider) experienced internal infrastructure or capacity failures starting at 13:40 independent of client traffic volume.

hypotheses.title: Auth-Service v7.1.3 Deployment Bug / Integration Interaction
hypotheses.mechanism: The deployment of auth-service v7.1.3 at 13:05 introduced a defect or bad retry/rate-limiting logic that either triggered the OTP failures or caused requests to be incorrectly flagged or rejected.

supporting.note: auth-service v7.1.3 was deployed 35 minutes prior to the onset at 13:05 with changes to limit OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes.
auth-service logged that OTP resend limits were reached starting at 13:42.

contradicting.note: The primary error is an explicit 503 Service Unavailable returned by otp-provider, and otp-provider metrics independently confirm severe vendor-side degradation starting at the exact same minute (13:40).

assumptions: The new retry/rate-limit logic in v7.1.3 somehow triggered or coincided with downstream provider rejection.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: Addressing the Critic's point, r2-observability-1 provided explicit health metrics for otp-provider confirming that its error rate spiked to 80% and p99 latency jumped to nearly 5.5s starting precisely at 13:40:00+00:00. This validates H1 conclusively, making it the primary hypothesis. H2 is retained with lower confidence as an alternative explanation, though undermined by the explicit 503 errors and vendor metric degradation.

issues: The top hypothesis H1 (otp-provider outage) has no direct telemetry retrieved for otp-provider itself, leaving its own health unverified as noted by automatic checks.
